title: How Voice AI Handles Shopify and Recharge Subscription Calls With Gorgias Handoffs
summary: Learn how voice AI handles Shopify and Recharge support calls, verifies callers, and routes complex cases to human agents using Gorgias.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- This guide covers a phone-first workflow for subscription brands that use Shopify for orders, Recharge for subscriptions, and Gorgias for human support.
- SigmaMind AI describes[Shopify customer and order lookups](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) and[Recharge subscription lookups](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) . Confirm the available fields and live-call behavior in your configuration.
- Gorgias ticket creation and call-summary sync require a configured integration or middleware. Confirm which Recharge subscription changes the configured agent can make before enabling them.
- The workflow suits brands with substantial inbound phone volume. A chat-first brand with few calls may have little reason to build it.


## Who this workflow is for


For brands with substantial inbound phone volume, this workflow connects routine Shopify order and Recharge subscription lookups to a human handoff in Gorgias when the voice agent cannot resolve a call. If your support agents spend peak periods answering tracking and renewal questions, a voice agent could answer questions supported by verified account records and transfer unresolved calls to a person.


The guide assumes you already use Gorgias for support tickets and have a phone system that can route calls to human agents. SigmaMind AI fits operations that want voice AI alongside an existing telephony stack, but you would need to configure how call context reaches Gorgias. If most customers contact you through chat and phone calls are rare, the integration work may outweigh the value of automating those calls.


## The three systems and what each one is responsible for


Shopify supplies the order and fulfillment information needed to answer questions such as whether an order has shipped. SigmaMind AI[describes its Shopify connector](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) as fetching customer profiles, order status, and basic fulfillment details. Its published description does not document order-changing actions. Shopify’s[Admin API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) uses access tokens with requested scopes, so you should limit the agent’s access to the data needed for order lookups.


Recharge supplies subscription details and delivery schedules. SigmaMind AI[describes its Recharge connector](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) as retrieving active subscriptions and plan details, and says agents can modify subscriptions. Before enabling a pause or date change, you need to confirm the connector’s permissions and the caller-confirmation steps. Check the applicable[Recharge API permissions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) and give routine lookups read access without granting write access for subscription or payment changes.


Gorgias can hold the support ticket and approved lookup context for a human agent, but the phone transfer and the ticket update are separate steps. SigmaMind AI[lists Gorgias in its app library](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) , but the available documentation does not establish a ready-made ticket or call-summary sync for this workflow. You need to configure and test that context transfer separately from the phone transfer.


The cited materials do not document a ready-made three-way workflow for Shopify, Recharge, and Gorgias. Confirm how your configured integrations, APIs, or middleware will match records and pass call context between them.


## Step-by-step: how a call moves through the system


1.


SigmaMind AI answers the call and uses a phone number or email address to find a possible customer record. If several records match, the agent can request another identifier, such as an order number. Before disclosing account details, it must apply your configured identity-verification check. An order number or record match alone does not prove that the caller owns the account.


2.


The agent retrieves the information needed for the question. SigmaMind AI documents a[Shopify connection](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) that fetches orders and fulfillment details, and a[Recharge connection](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) that fetches active subscriptions and plan details. Configure the call flow to request current records, and confirm which fields each connection returns during a live call.


3.


The agent answers questions that the retrieved records support. For example, it can give an order status when Shopify returns one or tell a caller which subscription plan Recharge shows. A request to pause a subscription needs a separate decision. Recharge offers write actions, but you must confirm the enabled action, its permissions, and the caller-confirmation step before letting the agent make a change.


4.


The agent transfers calls it cannot safely resolve. Conflicting records, failed lookups, billing disputes, refund requests, and payment-method changes should not produce a guessed answer or an assumed account action. The call flow should tell the caller that a human agent will take over.


5.


The human agent needs the reason for transfer and the results of any successful lookups. Configure the transfer to pass the verified customer identifier, relevant order or subscription, caller request, and any lookup failure to the human agent. Separately configure and test which approved details reach Gorgias. SigmaMind AI[lists Gorgias as an integration](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) , but its published materials do not document a ready-made Shopify, Recharge, and Gorgias handoff. Confirm the Gorgias ticket-creation and call-summary path through tool configuration, webhooks, or middleware before relying on it.


## Caller identification and data permissions


A phone or email match should locate a customer record, not authorize access to it. SigmaMind AI says its[Shopify integration](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) can identify customers by phone or email and retrieve order information. Its[Recharge integration](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) describes customer and subscription lookups. Your implementation must confirm how it links the two records and handles missing or duplicate matches. A caller may know someone else’s email or call from a spoofed number, so a match alone should not release account details.


Give the voice agent only the permissions it needs to answer approved questions. Shopify requires apps to request[specific access scopes](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) . Recharge separates[read permissions for customers, orders, and subscriptions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) from write permissions for actions such as changing a subscription or payment method. Use scoped, read-only credentials for lookups, and reserve write access for actions you have explicitly configured and approved.


The available SigmaMind AI integration descriptions do not define a verification threshold for billing changes. Before enabling any sensitive action, decide what additional proof the caller must provide, whether the caller must confirm the proposed change, and when a human must take over. If the agent cannot verify the caller under your policy, it should withhold account details and transfer the call.


## Example call scenarios


An order-status call can end with the voice agent when the Shopify lookup returns current fulfillment details. For example, a caller asks, “Where is order 1042?” If the caller passes the configured check and Shopify returns a shipment date and tracking number, the agent could relay those returned details. For example, it might say, “Your order shipped Tuesday. The tracking number ends in 4821.” SigmaMind AI[documents order and fulfillment lookups](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) . If the lookup returns no tracking details, the agent should say so rather than invent an update.


A subscription skip request depends on which Recharge actions the implementation permits. A caller asks, “Can I skip next month’s delivery?” The agent checks the subscription and, if the configured lookup returns it, the next scheduled charge. If you have verified and enabled the specific skip action, the agent can confirm the requested date before making the change. Otherwise, it can explain the schedule and transfer the request. SigmaMind AI[describes subscription changes](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) , but its published post does not specify the write permissions or confirmation steps.


A failed-payment question can require a human even when the agent can find the account. A caller says, “Why did you charge me again after my payment failed in January?” The agent should not decide a dispute from a subscription lookup alone. Your implementation must confirm which charge history it can retrieve and transfer questions that require investigation, refunds, or payment-method changes with the caller’s question and approved account context.


An account restriction or failed lookup should stop an automated subscription change. A caller says, “My account is locked, but I need to change my subscription today.” If a separately configured account-status check identifies a restriction, or a Shopify lookup returns an access error, the agent should avoid guessing at the cause and transfer the request to a human. An API error alone does not establish a fraud flag or explain why an account is locked. Sending a summary into Gorgias requires a separately configured and tested handoff.


## Escalation criteria and the handoff to Gorgias


Transfer a call when the agent cannot resolve it through permitted lookups or the caller requests an action outside its approved scope. Billing disputes that require charge investigation, refund requests, fraud flags, and payment-method changes all warrant a human agent. A locked account, failed customer match, or Shopify or Recharge API error should also stop automated handling. For a failed payment, the agent can relay a status it can retrieve, but a human should handle questions that require a billing decision.


Before bridging the call, SigmaMind AI’s[warm-transfer approach](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) describes preparing a summary and passing context variables to the receiving agent. For a subscription pause request, those details could include the matched customer record, the subscription in question, and why the agent could not complete the request. If your phone-transfer configuration supports a private whisper, it can give the human agent that context while the caller remains on the line. Keep payment credentials out of the summary.


A voice transfer does not automatically create a Gorgias ticket or place the summary in one. If you need that context in Gorgias, configure and test middleware or an API workflow that matches the call to the right customer and writes the approved details. The available documentation does not establish a pre-built SigmaMind AI and Gorgias sync or confirm that a ticket will appear before the agent answers. Until you validate that timing, use the whisper for the live handoff and have the agent follow your existing ticket process.


## Operational safeguards for billing and account actions


Before enabling any subscription change, grant only the[Shopify access scopes](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) and[Recharge API permissions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) that the approved action requires. Define how the caller proves account ownership, how the agent confirms the requested change, and when a human must approve it. A phone number or email match alone should not authorize a billing change.


Transfer calls when an API cannot provide a reliable answer. Denied access, an unavailable Shopify shop, or an API rate limit can interrupt a live lookup. Recharge can also deny a request or limit its rate. In those cases, pass the caller’s question and the error category to a human agent rather than guessing or reading an API error aloud.


Route billing questions to a human when the available charge history does not support an answer. Confirm the history returned by your Recharge configuration before deciding which questions the agent may handle. Recharge documents refund and payment-related API actions, but that does not establish that SigmaMind AI enables them in this voice workflow. Keep refunds and payment-method changes with a human unless you have confirmed the integration, permissions, and caller-verification controls.


## Implementation checklist


- \[ \] Confirm that SigmaMind AI can match a caller to the correct Shopify customer and Recharge subscription. Test duplicate phone numbers, mismatched email addresses, and records that appear in only one system.
- \[ \] Set a verification threshold before the agent reads account details. Require a stronger check for sensitive actions, and document when the agent must transfer instead.
- \[ \] Start with read-only access for order and subscription lookups. Confirm which Recharge write actions are enabled in your configuration, which require API or middleware work, and which remain human-only.
- \[ \] Confirm how a Gorgias ticket receives the call summary and account context. Test whether the handoff creates a ticket, updates an existing one, or supplies context only to the human agent.
- \[ \] Test failed lookups, denied access, locked accounts, and rate-limit responses. Make sure the agent stops the affected action and transfers the caller rather than guessing or reading an API error aloud.
- \[ \] Test live lookup latency at expected call volume. Check applicable[Shopify Admin GraphQL API limits](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) and[Recharge API documentation](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) for your configuration, and confirm that the agent handles slow, limited, or unavailable responses during a call.
- \[ \] Review SigmaMind AI’s[Shopify integration post](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) and[Recharge integration post](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) for the underlying connector details, then validate the configured actions in your own environment.


## Deciding whether to build this workflow


Estimate how many calls need a Shopify order lookup, a Recharge subscription lookup, or both before building the handoff. For example, a question about the next box may require both fulfillment and renewal information. If either lookup fails, the agent should transfer the call rather than guess.


SigmaMind AI fits brands that already handle substantial phone volume and need voice AI to work with their telephony setup. Its transfer options can pass call context to a person, while the Shopify, Recharge, and Gorgias data flow requires configuration and validation. Brands with frequent order and subscription calls may find that build worthwhile. Brands with few calls and mainly chat-based support should start with their chat workflow instead.
